verdict_basis: No material contradiction or important omission found in the exact supplied summary for base/core multiplayer 2–5 players after full source-text review and direct inspection of material PDF graphics. All six structure-bonus payout tables and scoring rates agree with the PDF.

scope.included: Base/core multiplayer, 2–5 players, using only the recovered English rulebook and its supplied text extraction.
excluded: Explicit optional variants including Delay of Game
Outside-source FAQ, errata and later revisions

method.description: Read all 234 lines of the exact summary and all 1656 lines of the source extraction, including all 32 primary-source pages. Cross-checked material procedures and quantities directly against rendered PDF graphics. Applied detailed source sections when quick reference text was abbreviated; did not infer correctness from the summary verification label. Dependency programs/libraries used only to read/render the supplied PDF and compute/write this report.

reviewed_claim_groups.detail: The summary explicitly scopes its teaching to base/core multiplayer 2–5 players and excludes solo, expansion, promo and optional variant rules. Greatest final fortune, clockwise individual turns without rounds, sixth-star immediate ending and possibility of a different scoring winner are preserved.

Faction piece quantities, random mat allocation, clockwise faction seating, shuffled decks, player-count-plus-one unseen Factory selection, random face-up structure tile, 11 encounter locations, two adjacent starting workers and all mat placements agree. Power/combat cards come from the Faction Mat; popularity/coins/two objectives come from the Player Mat. Lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
reviewed_claim_groups.visual_verification: Pages 7–9: starting indicators, covered technology/worker/recruit spaces, stars/mechs and empty one-time recruit spaces inspected.

reviewed_claim_groups.detail: Hand size public and combat-card content secret, exception allowing concealment of commitment during combat, secret objectives and coin-total disclosure rule are faithfully stated.

Mandatory token movement, optional top then optional bottom, no reversal, once-per-turn action limit, full exposed red cost before optional exposed green benefits, top gains funding bottom costs and practical overlap of noninteractive bottom decisions agree. Rusviet repeat-section exception does not create unlimited actions.
reviewed_claim_groups.visual_verification: Page 10 full mat/zoom and page 14 upgrade diagram inspected.

reviewed_claim_groups.detail: Units or unoccupied owned structures control; enemy workers take control over a structure; resources belong to the territory controller; defender retains temporary control during pending combat. Structures retain owner abilities except uncontrolled Mill. Resource transport/spending, unlimited resource supply, workers not resources and home-base exclusion are covered.

Two different units moving sequentially one territory each or one coin before upgrades; no independent worker entry into opposing-worker territory or entry/exit through opposing plastic; only mechs carry workers; carrying does not consume worker movement; resources may be carried by all units. Entry stops and Speed restrictions are correct.
reviewed_claim_groups.visual_verification: Page 11 Move diagram and lake/river/tunnel map inspected.

reviewed_claim_groups.detail: Default water restrictions, lake shore adjacency, printed-tunnel adjacency for all units, private Mine usable despite enemy control, Speed tunnel-step accounting and Factory Move access agree. Lake carriage, no abandoned workers/resources, lake combat and no lake construction/deployment restrictions are included.

One coin pays for two power or one combat card, or for two chosen resources or one popularity respectively before upgrades. Trade resources require a controlled worker territory; all workers home prevents that branch. Empty combat deck recycle/exhaustion and Armory/Monument additional benefits are correct.

Full current exposed payment precedes production; choose up to two distinct controlled territories before upgrade; each worker can produce one token of correct terrain type. New workers come left-to-right after paying and affect later costs. Workers remain off the mat; partial/declined benefits permitted. Mill adds a territory and a worker-equivalent output alongside actual workers, also without a worker; upgraded allowance plus Mill can reach four.
reviewed_claim_groups.visual_verification: Page 13 worker-covered and exposed cost diagrams and terrain table; page 14 three-territory upgrade; page 18 Mill description inspected. The source graphic associates mountain/metal, farm/food, tundra/oil, forest/wood, village/worker and blank lake/Factory output.

reviewed_claim_groups.detail: Oil/metal/wood/food mapping, mat-dependent full resource costs and coins, optional coins, continued paid use after exhausting primary benefits, any green technology cube to empty bracketed red cost and fixed-border exclusion agree. The summary appropriately directs readers to their own mat rather than inventing universal costs.

Worker-containing controlled destination, free mech choice and immediate unlock applying to character/all mechs, no workers, are correct. One structure globally per territory, Factory build permission, home/lake exclusions, permanence and future top-action benefits agree.

Recruit taken from any bottom section to any open permanent one-time space for two power/coins/popularity/cards; ongoing bonus determined by removal location. Neighbor triggers, active-left-right order, two-player once-only rule, announcement and exclusion of top/Factory/encounter triggers are present.
reviewed_claim_groups.visual_verification: Page 10 complete mat shows Upgrade→1 power, Deploy→1 coin, Build→1 popularity, Enlist→1 card. Page 20 verifies four one-time two-unit bonuses and independent recruitment placement.

reviewed_claim_groups.detail: All five special abilities and relevant limits agree: Relentless includes Factory; Coercion once per turn and one resource irrespective of card value; Swim only workers/rivers; Meander distinct options ordered and first benefit usable for second cost; Dominate both objectives/unlimited combat stars up to six tokens.

All five faction destination pairs agree. Nordic worker Swim is distinguished from unlocked plastic Riverwalk. Speed applies to each selected plastic unit, not workers, with entry stops overriding extra distance.

reviewed_claim_groups.claim_group: Saxony and Rusviet other mech abilities
reviewed_claim_groups.detail: Underpass controlled mountains/tunnels/Mine and Township controlled villages/Factory are faithfully summarized. Disarm is tunnel/Mine-only once per combat. People’s Army adds one card total with any workers and still requires plastic; supplied two-mech/three-worker example matches.

reviewed_claim_groups.claim_group: Nordic, Crimea and Polania other mech abilities
reviewed_claim_groups.detail: Seaworthy adjacent-lake retreat and transport, Artillery one-power payment/two-power loss once per combat, Wayfare own/inactive bases including expansion placeholders, Scout random card theft once per combat, Submerge lake-to-lake movement, and Camaraderie combat-aggressor-only protection all agree. Polania receives no extra retreat permission.

All movement before combats and combats before bottom action; attacker picks combat order and uses combat ability first. Simultaneous secret dial 0–min(7,current power), plastic-based optional cards even at zero dial, tie to attacker, both players pay dial/discard cards without extra track debit, winner control and stars, retreat all defeated units leaving resources, aggressor worker popularity and loser-card condition all covered.

Normal two combat stars and Saxony compulsory victory stars are correct. Sixth-star termination, no later combat/encounter/action and return of initiating units in unresolved attacks agree. Bottom-row primary benefit/coins/own ongoing bonus before its sixth star and neighbor ordering/cutoff are explicitly stated.

Only character, movement stops for rest of turn, finish all Move/combat first, token survives defeat, public art/capitalized text, mandatory affordable selection except Meander up-to-two, full cost/partial benefit, all physical gains on encounter territory, isolated normal costs/bonuses and face-down bottom discard agree.

Each character’s first completed Move to Factory gives mandatory permanent selection, one card per player. Fifth action section follows ordinary optional top-then-bottom and repeat rule. Mat bonuses do not transfer. Bottom Move is one unit up to two territories, three with plastic Speed, with normal stops and Mine access. Factory produces nothing and scores three territories.

Own-turn before/after completed actions, all conditions at reveal, option to wait, one normal objective star, bottom-deck discard of both and Saxony retention agree. Nonbinding deals, only tangible coins exchangeable, tournament restriction and no canceling initiated combat are source-supported.

All nine categories and quantities agree: six upgrades, four mechs, four structures, four recruits, eight workers, revealed objective, up to two combat victories, eighteen popularity, sixteen power. Mandatory awards, shared categories and permanent stars despite later track reductions preserved.

Held coins plus popularity-based star, territory and complete pooled resource-pair income plus selected structure bonus are correct. Lakes count, home bases excluded, Factory exactly three, odd resource ignored, structures eligible despite enemy control. Tiebreaks exactly match detailed p29: workers+mechs+structures (exclude character), power, popularity, controlled resources, controlled territories, placed stars.
reviewed_claim_groups.visual_verification: Page 29 scoring track confirms popularity 0–6 pays 3/2/1, 7–12 pays 4/3/2, 13–18 pays 5/4/3 for stars/territories/resource-pairs.

reviewed_claim_groups.detail: All six tile conditions and every payout agree; adjacency features count uniquely across structures, removed encounter tokens still count, printed tunnels exclude Mine, longest continuous straight row only, combined farms/tundras. Rivers do not interrupt relevant adjacency/row; zero qualifiers earns zero.
reviewed_claim_groups.visual_verification: Page 19 inspected all six tiles: adjacent tunnels 1→2, 2–3→4, 4–5→6, 6→9; adjacent lakes and encounters same through 4–5, 6–7→9; on tunnels 1→2, 2→4, 3–4→6; straight row and farms/tundras 1→2, 2→4, 3→6, 4→9. Page 29 tunnel example also inspected.

important_omission_assessment.assessment: The summary covers setup, legal choices and costs, default and upgraded actions, control and transportation, all starting faction abilities and core mech abilities, combat and retreat, encounters/Factory/objectives, stars and ending priorities, all final scoring rates, all six structure bonuses and all tiebreakers. Referring to the player’s actual mat for varying exposed costs and upgrade benefits is sufficient; a summary need not reproduce each full mat.
nonessential_source_content_not_reproduc: Full global component inventory counts and combat deck value distribution
Designer strategy notes and teaching suggestions
Power-dial assembly and publisher contact/promotional information
important_omission_assessment.reason_not_material: These do not remove a necessary rule for ordinary scoped play. Physical cards and mats remain the primary interfaces for their own printed benefits and costs.

source_interpretation_notes.note: The quick reference abbreviates objective timing as any time; detailed p26 expressly limits reveal to the player’s own turn before/after actions. Summary follows the detailed rule.
Page 28 describes 18 popularity as using the 13–17 level; p29 graphic places 18 in the same top scoring band. Summary’s 13–18 band faithfully expresses that scoring rule.
Summary uses explicit active/left/right recruit resolution from p20 along with p28 sixth-star priority; this is supported by the supplied source.

limitations: Audit assesses the supplied recovered rulebook only; it makes no claim about later official rulings or revisions.
Summary remains a rules summary used with physical game components; every card and all five full mat layouts are not reproduced in the source or summary.
Primary text was reviewed through its supplied complete extraction; visually material PDF diagrams were separately inspected rather than every decorative image.
